title: The Plants That Ate Lunch
intro: This quiz follows Nia and Kai as they discover how carnivorous plants trap insects to get extra nutrients.

questions.prompt: Why do carnivorous plants trap insects?
choices: To get extra nutrients from nutrient-poor soil
To make sunlight
To produce more water
To protect themselves from rain
questions.explanation: Carnivorous plants trap insects to get extra nutrients from nutrient-poor soil.

questions.prompt: What causes a Venus flytrap to snap shut?
choices: Its roots touch water
An insect touches the trigger hairs more than once
Sunlight reaches its leaves
The wind shakes the plant
questions.explanation: A Venus flytrap snaps shut when an insect touches the trigger hairs more than once.

questions.prompt: How does a Venus flytrap digest an insect?
choices: It chews the insect with teeth
It releases digestive juices that break the insect down
It swallows the insect whole
It dries the insect in sunlight
questions.explanation: A Venus flytrap releases digestive juices that break the insect down.

questions.prompt: How do pitcher plants and sundews trap insects?
choices: Pitcher plants use cup-shaped leaves, while sundews use sticky drops
Both use underground roots
Pitcher plants use thorns, while sundews use flowers
Both chase insects across the ground
questions.explanation: Pitcher plants use cup-shaped leaves, while sundews use sticky drops to trap insects.

questions.prompt: Why are carnivorous plants still called producers?
choices: They produce insects
They make their own sugar using sunlight
They eat only animals
They do not need water or air
questions.explanation: Carnivorous plants are still called producers because they make their own sugar using sunlight.
